requirements_slice.system_goal: Rerun the already-approved Week dev indicator helper slice as a local dev-only runtime diagnostics disclosure without widening scope and without forcing invalid canonical observability ownership.

in_scope.item: Keep the existing Week dev/prod chip visually compact.
In dev mode only, tapping the chip expands a lightweight local diagnostics block.
Show only render path, bootstrap result, and current mode from existing runtime/debug state.
Keep the diagnostics block local to the chip area with minimal layout shift.
Use packet-local frontend verification and visual evidence for dev-expanded and prod-unchanged Week states.

out_of_scope.item: No new top-level debug banner or separate diagnostics screen.
No correlation, trace, or payload diagnostics in user-facing UI.
No changes to Day screen or other product surfaces.
No canonical today-week closeout ownership in this rerun wave.

use_case.summary: Re-run the bounded Week helper disclosure from the existing compact chip and close it with packet-local evidence only.
use_case.scenario: On /week in non-production, tapping the compact chip expands a local disclosure with Week render path, bootstrap result, and runtime mode.
Tapping the compact chip again collapses the local disclosure without changing the Week product surface.
In production, and on non-Week routes, the chip remains visually unchanged and inert and no Week diagnostics block appears.
Visual evidence shows dev-collapsed, dev-expanded, and prod-unchanged Week states with the Week top area staying local and not banner-like.
Post-test review records a packet-local read-only verdict for the rerun and may be classified as clean or degraded-but-expected without claiming canonical Today/Week ownership.

business_invariants.invariant: This rerun extends the existing Week helper slice; it does not introduce a new product slice boundary or any backend contract.
The disclosure is client-local helper UI only and must not add backend requests, backend payload fields, or proxy routes.
Only render path, bootstrap result, and current mode may appear in the visible disclosure body.
Interactive behavior is limited to non-production on /week; production and non-Week routes remain inert.
Week render-path labels are derived from existing Week page states rather than new backend DTO fields or diagnostics endpoints.
Evidence ownership for this rerun is packet_local only; no canonical_flow_commands are owned here.
Visual proof for this rerun is stored under frontend/docs/review_evidence/front/day-week/2026-04-15-week-runtime-indicator.

expected_failure_handling.item: If any diagnostics source is absent, render a stable unknown or unavailable value instead of blocking /week.
If the page is between Week states, the disclosure may show loading or unknown, but it must not crash, leak raw objects, or call backend fallback endpoints.
If the shell-owned badge cannot remain route-gated to /week without altering Day or other routes, stop and escalate before widening the feature.

If packet-local post-test review lacks canonical Today/Week emission, the verdict may be degraded-but-expected only when Week-local request and visual identifiers remain attributable and no unexpected Week degradation appears.
If packet-local evidence is missing entirely or shows unexpected Week degradation, the wave remains blocked.

known_defects.defect: This rerun exists because earlier clean-slice artifacts left evidence ownership and review-evidence pathing too loose; the rerun corrects the architect contract without changing the approved Week helper behavior.

success_criteria.criterion: In dev mode on Week, tapping the current dev indicator expands a compact diagnostics block.
The diagnostics block shows render path, bootstrap result, and current mode only.
Tapping the dev indicator again collapses the diagnostics block.
In prod mode, the indicator remains inert and the visible UI stays unchanged.
No backend payload, scoring, explainability, WeekBrief, or business-logic changes are introduced.
Visual evidence shows the Week top area remains clean, local, and not banner-like.
Packet-local observability verdict is explicit and is not unexpected-degradation or no-evidence-blocker.
